name: Electrical Systems Technology AAS (A35130)
sourceWorkbook: Pitt CC: the 2025–26 Program CIP Codes list (credential codes, CIP 46.0302), the catalog's AAS page as indexed (68 credits, five semesters), the Electrical Systems Technology diploma-and-certificates page (course lists), the high-school options page (Technical Academy sections, Mon–Fri 9–11 AM), the Careers Electric Academy page, the faculty page (Vernon E. White Building), the 2026–27 Curriculum Academic Calendar, the NCCCS apprenticeship directory entry #97754 and the Thomas Electrical Solutions apprenticeship page; course hours and credits from the NCCCS Combined Course Library; sequences laid out to the published totals — compiled 2026-11-10
note: Five semesters over two years, 68 credits (the catalog's total): the diploma's courses — DC/AC theory, residential, commercial and industrial wiring, the NEC and its calculations, motors and controls, diagrams, print reading, industrial safety, application software and the applications project — with the PLC, digital electronics and photovoltaic courses of the college's certificates, ENG 111, MAT 110, ACA 111, a communication choice (COM 231 or ENG 112), a humanities/fine-arts and a social/behavioral-science choice, and two credits of the catalog's "Take One" options not read. The catalog's DC/AC option (ELC 112 at 5 credits or a 4-credit alternative) and safety elective are carried as ELC 112 and ISC 112, as the diploma lists them. Laid out from the college's published course lists to its published total; not yet confirmed against the catalog's program of study (catalog.pittcc.edu was unreachable on 2026-11-10). Class size 16 is a stand-in (the college publishes no section cap; its page says "small class sizes"). Faculty load is the workspace default (16 contact hours of a 40-hour week) — the college publishes no load.
weeklyHoursNote: Term hours per student are the catalog's weekly contact hours × 16 (the 16-week basis), whatever the term's length: the sessions carry them, the posted days, times and rooms place them. Hours and credits are the NCCCS course standard's; the high-school Technical Academy sits on the college's published Mon–Fri 9–11 AM block, every other course carries its hours with no section on record in the Vernon E. White Building; clinical hours are zero in every course.
